s1.syndrome_frame: Sepsis syndrome with cardiovascular and respiratory involvement
salient_findings: Positive blood cultures with gram-negative bacilli
key_facts: 56-year-old female with type 2 diabetes
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Nonischemic cardiomyopathy with ejection fraction 25-34%
Receiving milrinone through a double lumen tunneled catheter
Implantable cardioverter defibrillator placed 5 years prior
Disabled for 12 years
Developed cough and chills 4 days before presentation
Shortness of breath, weakness, and increased lower extremity edema 3 days later
Afebrile and hemodynamically stable on room air initially
Later developed fever and sinus tachycardia
Tunneled catheter site showed no signs of infection
Leukocyte count 12.4 ×10³/µL
C-reactive protein 158 mg/L
Urinalysis negative for leukocyte or nitrites
Chest radiograph showed no consolidation
Blood cultures positive for gram-negative bacilli

shortlist.label: Gram-negative sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has gram-negative bacilli in blood cultures and symptoms of sepsis

shortlist.label: Catheter-related bloodstream infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a tunneled catheter and developed sepsis, which is a common complication of catheter use

shortlist.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has gram-negative bacilli in blood cultures and Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a common cause of bacteremia in patients with catheters

shortlist.label: Escherichia coli sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Escherichia coli is a common cause of gram-negative sepsis and patient has symptoms of sepsis

shortlist.why_kept: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a common cause of gram-negative bacteremia and patient has symptoms of sepsis

raw.rationale: The patient had a double lumen tunneled catheter and developed symptoms of infection such as fever and increased leukocyte count, with blood cultures positive for gram-negative bacilli from both the catheter and peripheral sites, indicating a catheter-related infection.

rejected.label: Gram-negative sepsis
rejected.why: While the patient has gram-negative sepsis, the presence of a catheter and positive blood cultures from the catheter site suggest a more specific diagnosis of catheter-related bloodstream infection.

rejected.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence to suggest Pseudomonas aeruginosa as the causative organism over other gram-negative bacilli.

rejected.why: There is no specific evidence to suggest Escherichia coli as the causative organism over other gram-negative bacilli.
